# How to translate this chunk

This file holds `items`, a list of `{"k", "ctx", "t"}`. `t` is English text
that a reader of an Indian app or website sees. `ctx` is the field it came
from, such as label, hint, button, documents, brief or title. Use it to judge
tone and length: a label stays short, a hint can be a sentence.

Write `{"items": [{"k": ..., "t": ...}, ...]}` to the path in `write_to`.
Keep every `k` unchanged and in the same order. Put the translation in `t`.
Leave out `ctx`. Do not add, merge, split or drop items.

## Keep these exactly as they are

- Placeholders and markup: `{0}`, `{name}`, `%s`, `%d`, `%1$s`, HTML tags, `\n`.
- Website addresses, e-mail addresses and links.
- Every number: phone and toll-free numbers, Aadhaar, account, IFSC, PAN, PIN
  codes, amounts, dates, percentages. Write digits as 0-9, the Western digits,
  in every language, including Urdu. People type these into forms that take
  Western digits.
- Acronyms people know in Latin letters: OTP, PAN, IFSC, UPI, KYC, e-KYC, DBT,
  BPL, APL, NFSA, PM-KISAN, SMS, PDF, ID.

## Names

- Product, app, portal and scheme names: transliterate them into the script so
  they read naturally. Keep any acronym inside them in Latin, so "APPSC
  portal" becomes APPSC followed by the word for portal.
- A button or menu label quoted from a website, such as 'Apply Online' or
  'Register', stays in English inside quotes. The reader has to find that exact
  English word on the screen.
- People and places in examples are transliterated, never replaced with other
  names.
- Government office titles are transliterated so the reader can say them at
  the counter: Tahsildar, Patwari, Talathi, Mamlatdar, BDO, Collector, Gram
  Panchayat. The language notes below give the usual local forms.

## Tone

Write for an ordinary person who may be elderly and may have had little
schooling. Use everyday spoken language, not heavy official vocabulary. Where
people really say the English word, write it in the script: online, form,
portal, login, mobile, bank, certificate, download, upload, app. Keep
instructions short and direct, in the form "do this".

"Gender" means sex (male or female). It is never the word for caste.

## Before you write

Check that you have the same number of items as the input and that every
number and placeholder came through. Write the whole file in ONE Write call,
as valid UTF-8 JSON with no `\u` escapes and nothing else in the file.

## Hindi (hi)

Script: Devanagari. Used in UP, MP, Bihar, Rajasthan, Haryana, HP, Uttarakhand,
Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh and Delhi, and understood across the north.
Tone: everyday spoken Hindi (Hindustani). Avoid Sanskritised official words.
Words: ऑनलाइन, फॉर्म, पोर्टल, लॉगिन, आधार, बैंक, मोबाइल, OTP, हेल्पलाइन,
सर्टिफिकेट, डाउनलोड, अपलोड.
UI: आवेदन करें (Apply), जमा करें (Submit), आगे (Next), पीछे (Back), खोजें (Search),
शेयर करें (Share), सेटिंग (Settings), भाषा (Language), मदद (Help).
Offices: तहसीलदार, पटवारी, ग्राम पंचायत, कलेक्टर, ब्लॉक विकास कार्यालय (BDO).
Gender: लिंग (never जाति). Money: रु. 6,000; रु. 8 लाख. September: सितंबर.

## Gujarati (gu)

Script: Gujarati. Used in Gujarat, and spoken in Dadra & Nagar Haveli and
Daman & Diu.
Tone: everyday spoken Gujarati.
Words: ઓનલાઇન, ફોર્મ, પોર્ટલ, લૉગિન, આધાર, બેંક, મોબાઇલ, OTP, હેલ્પલાઇન, સર્ટિફિકેટ / દાખલો,
ડાઉનલોડ, અપલોડ.
UI: અરજી કરો, સબમિટ કરો, આગળ, પાછળ, શોધો, શેર કરો, સેટિંગ્સ, ભાષા, મદદ.
Offices: મામલતદાર, તલાટી, ગ્રામ પંચાયત, કલેક્ટર, તાલુકા પંચાયત.
Gender: જાતિ is caste; use લિંગ. Money: રૂ. 6,000; રૂ. 8 લાખ. September: સપ્ટેમ્બર.

## Marathi (mr)

Script: Devanagari. Used in Maharashtra, and widely in Goa.
Tone: everyday Marathi as spoken in Maharashtra.
Words: ऑनलाइन, फॉर्म, पोर्टल, लॉगिन, आधार, बँक, मोबाइल, OTP, हेल्पलाइन, दाखला / सर्टिफिकेट,
डाउनलोड, अपलोड.
UI: अर्ज करा, सबमिट करा, पुढे, मागे, शोधा, शेअर करा, सेटिंग्ज, भाषा, मदत.
Offices: तहसीलदार, तलाठी, ग्रामपंचायत, जिल्हाधिकारी (कलेक्टर), आपले सरकार सेवा केंद्र.
Gender: लिंग. Money: रु. 6,000; रु. 8 लाख. September: सप्टेंबर.

## Bengali (bn)

Script: Bengali. Used in West Bengal and Tripura, and in Assam's Barak Valley
and the Andamans.
Tone: everyday spoken Bengali (চলিত ভাষা), not সাধু ভাষা.
Words: অনলাইন, ফর্ম, পোর্টাল, লগইন, আধার, ব্যাংক, মোবাইল, OTP, হেল্পলাইন, সার্টিফিকেট,
ডাউনলোড, আপলোড.
UI: আবেদন করুন, জমা দিন, পরবর্তী, পিছনে, খুঁজুন, শেয়ার করুন, সেটিংস, ভাষা, সাহায্য.
Offices: বিডিও অফিস, গ্রাম পঞ্চায়েত, তহসিলদার, জেলাশাসক (কালেক্টর), দুয়ারে সরকার.
Gender: লিঙ্গ. Money: 6,000 টাকা; 8 লাখ টাকা. September: সেপ্টেম্বর.

items.t: Karnataka's health cover, run together with the central Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY. Families with a BPL (Priority Household or Antyodaya) ration card get free treatment up to Rs.5 lakh a year for the whole family; other families get 30% of the treatment cost paid, up to Rs.1.5 lakh a year. Treatment starts at a government hospital, which refers you to a listed private hospital if it cannot treat you; listed emergencies can go straight to a listed hospital. The card is made at a government hospital counter for Rs.10 with your Aadhaar and ration card.
BPL families: up to Rs.5 lakh a year free; other families: 30% of the cost, up to Rs.1.5 lakh a year
Every resident of Karnataka with an Aadhaar card can enrol
Eligible category (free treatment up to Rs.5 lakh per family per year): families with a Priority Household (BPL) or Antyodaya ration card under the Food Security Act
General category (APL card or no ration card): the government pays 30% of the package rate, up to Rs.1.5 lakh per family per year, and the family pays the rest
Simpler treatments are given only in government hospitals. A private hospital needs a referral from a government hospital, except for the listed emergencies
Aadhaar authentication is compulsory before a referral to a private hospital
Aadhaar card of the patient (each member of the family enrols separately)
Ration card, which decides whether you are in the eligible or the general category
Mobile number, for the SMS with your ArK ID
Rs.10 for the card (Rs.20 for a reprint if it is lost)
Referral letter from the government hospital, when going to a private hospital
Earlier prescriptions, test reports and discharge papers, if any

At the registration (Arogya Mitra) counter of any government hospital: Primary Health Centre, Community Health Centre, taluk or district hospital, or medical college hospital. Take every member's Aadhaar card and the ration card, and Rs.10 per card. Grama One, Karnataka One and Bangalore One centres also issue the card.
The patient's own Aadhaar. Each family member is enrolled one by one.
Authentication
Fingerprint
Fingerprint on the biometric device. If it fails, the staff can use an OTP to the Aadhaar mobile or the QR code on the Aadhaar card.
Ration card (PDS) number
From the ration card. It links you to your family in the food department's records.
Eligible patient (Priority Household card)
Filled automatically: Priority Household or Antyodaya card = Eligible; APL card or no card = General.
Name, gender and age
Lakshmamma Hanumanthappa, Female, 58
Taken from the Aadhaar e-KYC. Check the spelling before the card is printed.
Your ArK ID is sent here by SMS.
District / Taluk
Chitradurga / Hiriyur
Where you live.
Consent and self-declaration
Signed — no other health insurance scheme
A printed form: you allow your Aadhaar to be used for enrolment and state that you are not covered by another scheme.
ArK ID (generated)
Your ration card number, a dash and your member number. It is printed on the card.
Card fee
Rs.10 paid
Paid once. A reprint of a lost card costs Rs.20.
Go to the registration counter of a government hospital (PHC, CHC, taluk or district hospital) with your Aadhaar and ration card.
The staff check your Aadhaar by fingerprint (or OTP or QR code), and your ration card decides your category: Eligible (BPL) or General.
Sign the consent and self-declaration, pay Rs.10, and collect the printed card with your ArK ID. Repeat this for each family member.
When you fall ill, go first to a government hospital. If it cannot give the treatment, ask the doctor for a referral to a private hospital empanelled under AB-ArK.
At the private hospital, go to the Arogya Mitra desk with the card, your Aadhaar and the referral letter. The hospital takes approval from SAST; for eligible families the treatment is cashless.
In an emergency covered by the listed emergency procedures, go straight to the nearest empanelled hospital. No referral is needed.
If a hospital asks a BPL card holder to pay for a covered treatment, call 104 or 1800 425 8330 before paying.
104 — Arogya Sahayavani (toll free); 1800 425 8330 — Arogya Karnataka helpline
Karnataka Social Security Pensions (Old Age, Sandhya Suraksha, Widow and Disability Pension)
Directorate of Social Security and Pensions, Revenue Department, Government of Karnataka

Karnataka pays a monthly pension to poor elderly people, widows and people with disabilities, straight into a bank or post office account. The old age pension is Rs.600 a month from 60 to 64 and Rs.1,200 from 65; Sandhya Suraksha gives Rs.1,200 to farmers, labourers, weavers and fishermen aged 65 and above; widows get Rs.800; people with disabilities get Rs.800 to Rs.2,000. One common form covers all of them, and you hand it in at the Atalji Janasnehi Kendra (Nadakacheri) for your area.
Rs.600 to Rs.2,000 a month depending on the pension; Rs.1,200 for most people aged 65 and above
Resident of Karnataka, with a family income below Rs.32,000 a year
Old age pension (IGNOAPS): BPL, aged 60 or above. Rs.600 a month at 60 to 64, Rs.1,200 at 65 and above

Sandhya Suraksha: aged 65 or above; small or marginal farmer, farm labourer, weaver, fisherman or unorganised worker (not construction-board workers); husband and wife's deposits together not above Rs.10,000. Rs.1,200 a month
Widow pension: destitute widow aged 18 to 64. Rs.800 a month, until remarriage or a job that takes income above the limit
Disability pension: 40% disability or more, certified by a medical board, Rs.800; 75% or more, Rs.1,400; 75% or more mental disability, Rs.2,000
Not already drawing another pension. Having sons does not disqualify you if they do not support you
The filled application form
Age proof: birth certificate, voter ID with date of birth, or a doctor's age certificate
Residence certificate
Income certificate (below Rs.32,000 a year)
Bank or post office passbook, first page
As needed: husband's death certificate (widow), medical board disability certificate (disability), occupation certificate from the Tahsildar (Sandhya Suraksha)

The Atalji Janasnehi Kendra (Nadakacheri counter) at your hobli or taluk office. Take the filled form, signed or with your thumb impression, with copies of Aadhaar, age proof, residence and income certificates, the bank or post office passbook and the ration card, plus the death, disability or occupation certificate your pension needs. The counter charges a small service fee; ask for the printed acknowledgement.
Tumakuru / Sira / Gowdagere / Hosahalli
Written at the top of the form. It decides which village officer verifies your application.
Gangamma Siddappa
As on your Aadhaar.
Male or female
Tick or write one.
Siddappa (late)
Husband's name for a married woman or a widow, father's name otherwise.
Full postal address (present and permanent)
Door no. 7, Hosahalli, Sira taluk, Tumakuru 572137
Write both if you live away from your permanent home.
Age on the date of application
67 — voter ID attached
Write which age proof you are attaching.
Pension applied for
Sandhya Suraksha
Tick one box: old age, widow, disability, Sandhya Suraksha, Manaswini, Maithri, acid attack victim, farmer's widow or endosulfan victim.
Family's annual income
Must be below Rs.32,000. Attach the income certificate.
Combined deposits of husband and wife
Rs.4,500, savings account, Sira branch of a co-operative bank
Amount, type of deposit and the bank. For Sandhya Suraksha it must not be above Rs.10,000.
Any other pension, and occupation
No other pension; farm labourer (Tahsildar's certificate attached)
Another pension makes you ineligible. The occupation certificate is needed for Sandhya Suraksha.
Download the common pension form from dssp.karnataka.gov.in, or ask for it at the Nadakacheri counter.
Fill it in, tick the pension you want, sign or put your left thumb impression, and attach the documents.
Hand it in at the Atalji Janasnehi Kendra for your hobli or taluk, and keep the acknowledgement number.
The village administrative officer and the revenue inspector check your age, income and residence, often with a home visit. The Tahsildar then sanctions the pension.
The pension order gives you a beneficiary ID. The pension is then paid every month into your bank or post office account.

Check the status, or a stopped payment, on the Beneficiary Status page of dssp.karnataka.gov.in with your beneficiary ID. If payments stop, first make sure your account is seeded with Aadhaar, then go to the taluk office.
080-22232040 / 080-22232012 — Directorate of Social Security and Pensions, Bengaluru; 1902 — Karnataka government citizen helpline
Shakti Yojana (Free Bus Travel for Women)
Transport Department, Government of Karnataka — KSRTC, BMTC, KKRTC and NWKRTC

Women and girls who live in Karnataka, and transgender persons, travel free in ordinary government buses anywhere inside the state. There is no form, card or registration: show a government photo ID with a Karnataka address to the conductor and you get a zero-fare Shakti ticket. Air-conditioned and luxury buses, sleeper buses and buses that cross into another state are not free.
Free travel in ordinary and express non-AC government buses within Karnataka
Women and girls of any age who live in Karnataka, including school and college students
Transgender persons who live in Karnataka
No income, caste or age limit, and nothing to apply for
Covers ordinary and express non-AC buses of KSRTC, BMTC, KKRTC and NWKRTC, including non-AC electric buses
Not covered: Rajahamsa, AC buses such as Airavat, Vajra, Vayu Vajra, Ambaari and Flybus, sleeper buses, and interstate routes, even for the Karnataka part of the trip
Aadhaar card, or

There is no form and nowhere to apply. Board an ordinary or express non-AC bus of KSRTC, BMTC, KKRTC or NWKRTC on a route inside Karnataka, show the conductor an ID with your photo and Karnataka address (original, photocopy or DigiLocker copy), and ask for the Shakti ticket.

The ticket shows what the trip would have cost. The state pays this amount to the bus company.
Carry one ID with your photo and Karnataka address. Aadhaar is the easiest; a photocopy or the DigiLocker copy on your phone is also accepted.
Board an ordinary or express non-AC government bus. Check the name on the front: Rajahamsa, Airavat, Vajra, Vayu Vajra, Ambaari, Flybus and sleeper buses are not free.
Tell the conductor your destination, show the ID and ask for the Shakti ticket.
Take the zero-fare ticket and keep it until you get down. A passenger without a ticket can be fined even on a free trip.
On KSRTC, KKRTC and NWKRTC buses half the seats are kept for men; BMTC city buses have no such split.
If a conductor refuses the free ticket on a covered bus, note the bus number, route and time, and complain to that corporation's helpline.

Karnataka Construction Workers Labour Card (KBOCWWB e-Card)
Karnataka Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board, Labour Department, Government of Karnataka

Construction workers in Karnataka who register with the Welfare Board get a labour card, now a digital e-card, which opens the board's help: Rs.50,000 for each of a woman worker's first two deliveries, Rs.60,000 for a marriage, up to Rs.2 lakh for a major illness, education help for children, accident cover and a pension at 60. You register on the board's Karmika Seva Kendra (KSK) portal with your Aadhaar mobile number and a 90-day work certificate. Workers who already hold an old Seva Sindhu or e-Karmika card move it to the new portal with their registration and reference numbers.
Labour e-card for board help: Rs.50,000 per delivery, Rs.60,000 for marriage, up to Rs.2 lakh medical aid, pension up to Rs.3,000 a month at 60
Aged 18 to 60
Worked at least 90 days as a building or construction worker in the last 12 months: mason, helper, carpenter, painter, plumber, electrician, bar bender, tile layer and similar work
Working in Karnataka
The e-card is valid for one year. Renew it on the portal with a fresh work certificate, or the benefits stop
For the pension, you must have been registered for at least 3 years before turning 60

Yuva Nidhi (Unemployment Allowance for Graduates and Diploma Holders)
Skill Development, Entrepreneurship and Livelihood Department (Department of Employment and Training), Government of Karnataka

Karnataka pays a monthly allowance to young people who finished a degree or diploma and still have no job six months after the result: Rs.3,000 a month for graduates and postgraduates, Rs.1,500 for diploma holders. It is paid for up to two years, or until you get a job or start further studies, whichever comes first. You apply on Seva Sindhu (now Seva One), and you must confirm on the portal every three months that you are still unemployed, or the payment stops.
Rs.3,000 a month for graduates, Rs.1,500 a month for diploma holders, for up to 2 years
Passed a degree, postgraduate degree or diploma from the 2022-23 academic year onward
No job (government or private) and not self-employed for 180 days after the result

Submit and note the application number. The district employment officer checks your certificates; follow it with 'Yuvanidhi Application Status Check' on the portal.

When you get a job or join a course, stop declaring. The allowance ends after two years in any case.

Gruha Jyothi (Free Electricity up to 200 Units)
Energy Department, Government of Karnataka, through the electricity supply companies (BESCOM, MESCOM, CESC, HESCOM, GESCOM)

Karnataka gives every household free electricity up to its usual monthly use, as long as that stays within 200 units. Your free limit is your average monthly use in 2022-23 plus 10 units. Use within that limit and the bill is zero; use more and you pay only for the extra units; cross 200 units in a month and you pay the full bill for that month. You register once, free, by linking the house's electricity account to your Aadhaar. Owners and tenants can both apply.

Keep your latest electricity bill ready and find the ESCOM name and the Account ID on it.

Open sevasindhugs.karnataka.gov.in, choose Gruha Jyothi and click to register. The form opens without any login. A Grama One, Karnataka One or Bangalore One centre, or your ESCOM office, will also register you free.
Select your ESCOM, type the Account ID and check the name and address that appear. Choose Owner, Tenant or Family member, then enter your Aadhaar and verify it with the OTP.
Tick the declaration, submit, and note the acknowledgement number. You can check the status later on the Seva Sindhu 'Track Status' page.
From the next bill, your bill shows your free limit (eligible units). Within it the bill is zero; above it you pay only for the extra units; above 200 units you pay the whole bill.
Tenants moving house: use the Gruha Jyothi De-link option on the same portal to free your Aadhaar from the old connection, then register again at the new house.
